doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Getting a headphone mix before the artists put the phones on
summary: Hank asks players to wait while he builds a mix, and says an artist's comfort in the phones matters more than technical correctness.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah sure. If you have a good mix in the phones it gives the artist — whoever the artist might be — it might be with a guitar player in the room — you’ve got to make them all feel comfortable. The earphones are really important. You get that really good balance in the earphones — I would do things like guys would put on the phones immediately and start, “No, no, no.” I’d say, “Give me a chance to get a mix and we’ll work on the phones after that.” And generally that usually worked. Even at the beginning of the date they put the phones on but I’m just still getting a bass sound or I’m getting — you know it’s not really right yet you know. I would think, sometimes I’d say, “Don’t put on the phones yet, let me get a mix, I’ve got an earphone mix” I said, if they’re comfortable out there and they’re all kind of facing each other, the rhythm section especially, facing each other. If you’re working with a big band you can’t do that. If you have a band you have to have a lead singer or something like that you put them in the booth, that’s going to work, that’s going to be fine. But remember that artist is the one that’s going to dictate what the rest of the thing — I mean I’ve worked with guys like Vic Damone and — because I can’t think of anybody else right now — but you know you’ve got to make them feel comfortable. And they will tell you I mean I would always ask the artist, “Are you all right? Are you comfortable?” And sometimes you know they’d say, “I want to hear more piano” or I want to hear — you know you’ve got to make them feel comfortable. Even if that makes us wrong out there in the earphones, at least they’re comfortable. If they’re comfortable making the record then you’re fine.
